$comment: Curated tools, MCP servers, kits, and services Lumen suggests based on what you asked for and what the agent used. Matched by concept id, request keyword, package, or concept category. `whyForYou` is written to complete the sentence 'Worth a look because …'.

entries.title: Rive
entries.summary: A visual editor for interactive animations that exports a tiny runtime for the web, iOS, and Android.
entries.whyForYou: you are hand-coding motion — Rive lets you design the animation visually and skip most of the timing code.

entries.title: Lottie
entries.summary: Plays After Effects animations on the web as JSON, so complex illustrated motion stays small and sharp.
entries.whyForYou: illustrated or looping animations are far easier to ship as Lottie files than to rebuild in code.

entries.title: Motion (formerly Framer Motion)
entries.summary: An animation library built around React components, with layout and gesture animations handled for you.
entries.whyForYou: you are animating inside React — Motion removes most of the manual ref and cleanup work.

entries.title: Theatre.js
entries.summary: A visual timeline editor that sits on top of your own code, so you can tweak animation timing by dragging keyframes.
entries.whyForYou: tuning easing and timing by editing numbers is slow; a timeline UI gets you there much faster.

entries.title: Scroll-driven Animations (Chrome guide + demos)
entries.summary: A gallery of scroll-linked effects built with native CSS scroll-driven animations, no JavaScript library needed.
entries.whyForYou: some scroll effects now work in pure CSS, which is lighter and smoother than a JS scroll listener.

entries.title: Figma MCP server
entries.summary: Connects Cursor to Figma so the agent can read your real designs and push generated screens back into a file.
entries.whyForYou: the agent can build from your actual Figma frames instead of guessing at spacing, colour, and type.

entries.title: Mobbin
entries.summary: A searchable library of screenshots from real production apps, organised by flow and UI pattern.
entries.whyForYou: before designing a flow from scratch, it is much quicker to see how shipped apps already solve it.

entries.title: Tailwind CSS
entries.summary: Styles elements with small utility classes in your markup instead of separate stylesheets.
entries.whyForYou: you are writing a lot of custom CSS by hand, which utilities would make shorter and more consistent.

entries.title: Open Props
entries.summary: A ready-made set of CSS custom properties for spacing, colour, easing, and shadows.
entries.whyForYou: it gives you a consistent design-token scale without inventing every value yourself.

entries.title: Radix Primitives
entries.summary: Unstyled, accessible React components for menus, dialogs, tooltips, and other fiddly widgets.
entries.whyForYou: hand-built dropdowns and modals almost always miss keyboard and screen-reader behaviour that Radix handles.

entries.title: shadcn/ui
entries.summary: Copy-paste React components built on Radix and Tailwind that you own and restyle freely.
entries.whyForYou: you get a working component set to start from, without taking on a dependency you cannot customise.

entries.title: axe DevTools
entries.summary: A browser extension that audits a page for accessibility problems and explains how to fix each one.
entries.whyForYou: it catches contrast, label, and focus issues that are invisible until someone cannot use your site.

entries.title: Playwright
entries.summary: Drives a real browser to test your site end to end, and can record the test by watching you click.
entries.whyForYou: it turns the manual clicking you do after each change into a check that runs automatically.

entries.title: Vitest
entries.summary: A fast test runner for JavaScript and TypeScript projects that share a Vite config.
entries.whyForYou: small unit tests around your logic catch breakage sooner than clicking through the UI.

entries.title: Lighthouse
entries.summary: Built into Chrome DevTools; scores a page on performance, accessibility, and best practices.
entries.whyForYou: it turns vague 'feels slow' into a specific list of what to fix first.

entries.title: Squoosh and Sharp
entries.summary: Squoosh compresses images in the browser; Sharp does the same job in a build script.
entries.whyForYou: unoptimised images are usually the single biggest thing slowing a site down.

entries.title: Vercel
entries.summary: Hosts front-end projects with preview URLs for every branch and no server setup.
entries.whyForYou: a live preview link per change is much easier to review than describing what you built.

entries.title: Cloudflare Pages
entries.summary: Free static and edge hosting with generous bandwidth and built-in analytics.
entries.whyForYou: a strong free alternative if you want hosting that stays cheap as traffic grows.

entries.title: Astro
entries.summary: A site framework that ships almost no JavaScript by default and lets you drop in React where needed.
entries.whyForYou: for content-heavy or portfolio sites this is usually faster and simpler than a full app framework.

entries.title: Neon Postgres
entries.summary: Serverless Postgres with instant database branching, so each feature can have its own copy of the data.
entries.whyForYou: you are working with SQL — branching databases means you can experiment without risking real data.

entries.title: Drizzle ORM
entries.summary: Writes type-safe SQL in TypeScript and generates migrations from your schema.
entries.whyForYou: typed queries catch column and table mistakes before the code ever runs.

entries.title: Zod
entries.summary: Describes the shape of data once and validates it at runtime with matching TypeScript types.
entries.whyForYou: it stops malformed API responses and form input from turning into confusing downstream bugs.

entries.title: TanStack Query
entries.summary: Handles fetching, caching, retries, and refetching of server data in React.
entries.whyForYou: it replaces most hand-rolled loading and error state around data fetching.

entries.title: Sentry
entries.summary: Captures errors from real users with the stack trace and the steps that led to them.
entries.whyForYou: without it you only hear about bugs when someone remembers to tell you.

entries.title: PostHog
entries.summary: Product analytics with session replay and feature flags, generous free tier.
entries.whyForYou: watching where people actually get stuck beats guessing which part of the flow to improve.

entries.title: Resend and React Email
entries.summary: Sends transactional email, with templates you build as React components.
entries.whyForYou: email templates are notoriously painful in raw HTML; this keeps them in familiar code.

entries.title: Clerk
entries.summary: Drop-in sign-in, sign-up, and user management with prebuilt UI components.
entries.whyForYou: authentication is high-risk to hand-roll; a managed provider handles sessions and resets for you.

entries.title: Sanity
entries.summary: A hosted content backend with a customisable editing interface.
entries.whyForYou: it lets you change site copy and images without editing code or redeploying.

entries.title: Context.dev MCP
entries.summary: Gives the agent live web search, page scraping, brand data, and design-system extraction.
entries.whyForYou: the agent can look up current documentation and real sites instead of relying on memory.

entries.title: Cursor rules and skills
entries.summary: Reusable instruction files that teach the agent your conventions once instead of every chat.
entries.whyForYou: if you keep repeating the same guidance to the agent, a rule or skill makes it stick.

entries.title: Cursor hooks
entries.summary: Scripts that run on agent events, so you can log, audit, or block what the agent does.
entries.whyForYou: hooks are how you observe and constrain agent behaviour rather than trusting it blindly.

entries.title: Cursor Bugbot
entries.summary: Reviews pull requests automatically and comments on likely bugs before a human looks.
entries.whyForYou: an automated first-pass review catches obvious mistakes when you have nobody to review your code.

entries.title: GitHub Actions
entries.summary: Runs your tests, builds, and deploys automatically whenever you push code.
entries.whyForYou: it removes the chance of forgetting a build or test step before you ship.

entries.title: lazygit
entries.summary: A keyboard-driven visual interface for git that runs in the terminal.
entries.whyForYou: seeing branches and staged changes laid out makes git far less intimidating than raw commands.

entries.title: dotenvx
entries.summary: Loads and encrypts environment variables per project so secrets never sit in plain text.
entries.whyForYou: you are handling API keys and config — this keeps them out of your commits.

entries.title: Biome
entries.summary: One fast tool that both formats and lints JavaScript and TypeScript, replacing Prettier plus ESLint.
entries.whyForYou: a single formatter and linter means fewer config files and fewer style arguments.

entries.title: Storybook
entries.summary: Renders each component in isolation so you can see every state without clicking through the app.
entries.whyForYou: it is the fastest way to review and document a growing component library.

entries.title: React Three Fiber
entries.summary: Write Three.js 3D scenes as React components, with a large helper library in Drei.
entries.whyForYou: raw Three.js needs a lot of boilerplate that React Three Fiber handles for you.

entries.title: Spline
entries.summary: A browser-based 3D design tool that exports interactive scenes for the web.
entries.whyForYou: it gets you a usable 3D scene without learning a full 3D pipeline first.

entries.title: Excalidraw
entries.summary: Quick hand-drawn-style diagrams for architecture and flows, free and shareable.
entries.whyForYou: sketching the structure before building usually surfaces problems earlier than code does.
